newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Esso cuts run at Thai refinery by 10-15 pct in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Esso cuts run at Thai refinery by 10-15 pct in Oct.

text.p: Esso Thailand, an affiliate of U.S. oil major Exxon Corp, has cut crude runs in October at its 145,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) oil refinery by 10 to 15 percent, a company spokesman said on Friday.
He said poor refining margins and lower domestic demand are two reasons behind the cuts.
"Everybody knows that the margin is going down," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone. The refinery is located in Sri Racha.

Earlier this week, Adul Leelapatranurak, executive director of state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) told Reuters that margins were down to $4-$5 per barrel from the $6 level required to break even.
The Esso spokesman said: "The decision to cut crude runs is dependent on demand and because it is now the rainy season, demand is down."
The monsoon season in Thailand lasts from June until October.
"Runs were a little bit slowed down then (during the monsoon)," the spokesman said without giving details.
He could not say when crude throughputs would return to full capacity. "It depends on the demand and also the margins," he added.
Esso's 33-year-old refinery on Thailand's eastern seboard is the oldest in the country and is 87.5 percent owned by Exxon and 12.5 percent by Thailand's finance ministry.
